tagline.text: A fan-shaped waterfall hidden at the end of a muddy forest trail in Sibagat

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay New Tubigon, Sibagat, Agusan del Sur

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person, day trip from Butuan)

children.text: Pinandagatan Falls is a fan-shaped waterfall tucked into the forest behind New Tubigon village in Sibagat, Agusan del Sur. It is about 17m high and about 24m wide, and reaching it takes a motorcycle taxi ride and a muddy jungle trek, which makes it a true off-the-beaten-path adventure.

Pinandagatan Falls lies in the forest of Barangay New Tubigon, in the municipality of Sibagat, Agusan del Sur, in the Caraga region of northeastern Mindanao. Wikipedia describes it as a fan-type waterfall that drops in two tiers for a total of about 16.8m and averages about 24m in width. The name is said to come from
dagatan
, a Visayan word for "lake," which suggests the broad pool that collects below the falls.

The falls are known first of all for how far away they feel. Many travel blogs mention a bumpy, muddy route of 31 km. Accounts differ on whether that figure covers only the motorcycle leg or the whole trip, and another guide puts the distance from central Bayugan to the starting point at about
12km
. The exact number matters less than the fact that the road is partly unpaved and the last stretch must be done on foot, so this is not a convenient, ordinary tourist stop.
According to local accounts, you walk down a forest trail for about
30–45 minutes

from near the barangay hall, with repeated ups and downs and a small river to cross. Bloggers describe the forest growing thicker toward the falls, with large rocks and clear water along the way. The falls continue in several tiers deeper into the forest, so there is more to see than just the view from the bottom if you want to look at the upper levels.

It also helps to know that this destination is still being developed. The Sibagat local government is promoting the site as an ecotourism area, and a June 2024 provincial government report says funds were allocated through the Department of Tourism road program for the New Tubigon bridge and for concreting the access road. Access may get easier as the road improves, but much of the available information comes from reviews written several years ago, so it is safest to check the latest conditions before you go.
This fan-shaped waterfall is about
high and about

wide on average, falling in two tiers into a pool below. The flow varies a lot by season: it is strong after rain and gentler in the dry months. Local advice says early morning, when soft light filters through the trees, is better for photos than the high midday sun.

The falls do not end in a single drop; several tiers continue deeper into the forest. After enjoying the view from the pool below, you can look at the upper tiers within a safe range if you have the time and energy.

You ride a motorcycle taxi, called a habal-habal locally, up the mountain road. Many are modified motorcycles with wooden seats on the sides that carry people and luggage together, and the ride itself is half of the adventure.

The last stretch is a walk down a forest trail that includes crossing a small river. The path is often slippery, so you need shoes you can trust, and that effort makes arriving feel all the more rewarding.

Wikipedia reports that the falls are believed to be among the longest-running waterfalls in the Caraga region. That reputation for water that does not dry up through the year is one reason travelers seek it out.
New Tubigon is a remote village, and some visitors report being offered fruit by residents or trying local snacks such as boiled kamansi seeds along the way. Take your time and enjoy the village.

According to visitor reports, the barangay hall keeps a visitors' logbook and can arrange a guide. Because this is a remote forest trail, route guidance and safety checks go together, so be sure to stop by and register.
Take a van or bus from the Butuan bus terminal to Bayugan. The trip takes about
1 hour
, and leaving early gives you more breathing room on the way back.
Buy water, snacks, and a plastic waterproof bag at the market near the Bayugan terminal. Local reviews often advise wrapping your belongings in plastic to protect them from rain and dust.
Find a habal-habal near the San Juan terminal and ride to the New Tubigon barangay hall. Before negotiating, settle on the round-trip fare and the time you will be picked up.
Sign the visitors' log at the barangay hall and ask for a guide. Use the restroom beforehand if needed.
Walk down the forest trail to the falls. With the ups and downs and a small river crossing, it takes about
30–45 minutes
Take photos, rest, and eat your packed lunch at the foot of the falls. Judge the water volume and current before deciding whether to enter the water.
Start back with plenty of time, since the way up is harder than the way down. If rain begins, the trail turns slippery quickly.
Ride the habal-habal back to Bayugan, then check the last bus or van time to Butuan and head back.
This schedule is only an example. In practice it varies a lot with habal-habal connections and the weather that day, so adjust it with your guide on site.
Travel from Butuan to Bayugan, check in to your lodging, and prepare supplies at the town market.
Set out early by habal-habal for New Tubigon to avoid the midday heat and afternoon rain.
Spend plenty of time at the falls and take photos, and if there is time, greet the barangay residents.
Leave early after lunch, return to Bayugan, and continue to your next stop.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Butuan Airport (BXU). The flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
; whether flights operate and at what times changes by season, so check before booking.
From Butuan Airport, go into the city by tricycle or taxi.
You can also connect via Cebu or Davao, but layovers can be long.
Take a bus or van from the Butuan bus terminal to Bayugan. It takes about
1 hour
, and the fare is quoted at around ₱50~100 (older sources show about ₱50~60; subject to change).
If you are coming from Davao, you can take a bus from the Davao Overland Transport Terminal to Butuan and get off at Bayugan.

Near the Bayugan terminal, take a habal-habal to the New Tubigon barangay hall. According to reviews (₱120 in 2017, ₱100~150 in a recent guide; confirm the fare first) it was around ₱100~150, and the ride takes about
30 minutes
Because road paving and bridge work are under way along this stretch, check the latest conditions locally.

items.title: Walking from the barangay hall to the falls

children.text: From the barangay hall, walk down the forest trail for about
30–45 minutes
. Some reviews say it took up to an hour.
With a river crossing and many ups and downs, waterproof footwear and a stick to use as a walking staff are helpful.

The muddy, slippery forest trail is the main challenge at Pinandagatan Falls, so going in a less rainy period is safest. Caraga tends to be rainier from December to February and somewhat drier from March to May, but rain can fall here at any time of year.

One blogger noted that the falls did not overflow even in the rainy season, so avoiding rainy days matters more than the month. If it rained the day before, the trail is very slippery and many people reportedly fall.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The trail turns muddy easily, so postpone if rain is forecast
Good time for trekking; carry plenty of water for the exposed stretches
Flow may be higher but mountain trails are slippery, so check the weather

New Tubigon village has almost no formal lodging, so it is most practical to stay in Butuan or Bayugan. Butuan has the widest choice of hotels and restaurants and is close to the airport, making it a good base, while Bayugan is closer to the falls and better for an early start.

Assume there are no restaurants in the village and prepare a packed lunch and water at the Bayugan market. Some visitors mention being offered fruit by residents, so if you buy snacks, carry cash in small denominations.

Planning the schedule is usually the biggest worry for first-time visitors. A day trip that leaves Butuan at dawn and returns the same day becomes tight if the habal-habal connections go wrong. If this is your first visit, sleeping one night in Bayugan and setting out early the next morning is more relaxed and safer. Eat a hearty meal of local food in Bayugan town, and keep lunch at the falls simple with a packed meal and some fruit.
Before leaving, contact the barangay hall or the Sibagat local government tourism office to check current road conditions and costs.
Wrap your belongings in plastic inside your backpack to protect them from rain, dust, and river crossings.
Non-slip trekking shoes or sandals are best, and long pants are recommended because bare legs can get scratched by grass.
Bring plenty of water, since there are almost no shops nearby.
Agree with the habal-habal driver in advance on the return time, and settle the round-trip fare first.
Set out early in the morning to avoid afternoon showers.
Going with companions is safer and more fun. Walking a remote forest trail alone is not recommended.
Carry out all your trash. Environmental protection efforts are under way here.
Do not be tempted to climb to the upper tiers if you can avoid it. Go only as far as your guide says is safe, and do not enter the pool when the water volume is high.

If your schedule is tight, plan to stay at the falls for about an hour. The forest trail takes longer on the way up than on the way down, and in the mountains the sun sets early in the afternoon, so returning late is easy.
If it has rained or is about to rain, the forest trail becomes very slippery and the river level can change, so postpone your trip.
Most access information comes from reviews several years old, so fares and trail conditions may have changed. Check the latest announcements.
Mobile signal may be weak on the remote mountain trail, so tell family or your lodging your plan and expected return time before leaving.
Do not step backward on slippery rocks while taking photos. You must check the depth and current of the pool below the falls yourself.
Habal-habal sometimes carry more riders than seats allow, but for safety it is better not to crowd on.
You may get scratched by wild plants or bitten by insects, so bring long clothing and first-aid supplies.
No official entrance fee or operating hours have been confirmed. Check the latest notice from the Sibagat local government or ask at the barangay hall directly before you go.
This waterfall is in Bislig, Surigao del Sur, the province next to Agusan del Sur, and it is far from here, so it is best visited as a separate trip.
A gateway city where you can visit museums and historic sites. Adding a day here as a base makes a good complement to the waterfall trip.
Sibagat is described as having waterfalls, caves, and hot springs. Check with the local government for exact locations and conditions.
Sibagat holds the Bagat Festival every year around the first week of October. It pairs nicely with a visit if the dates line up, but confirm the dates each year.
